items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Asch recorded two numbers with the singer Josh White and the line-up was Mary Lou, myself, Eddie Dougherty on drums and Jimmy Butts on bass.

ctx.x: After a few rehearsals with Mary Lou, we recorded for a small company called Asch records. One of the best numbers of the six we recorded was 'Night and Day'. The three of us had put our ideas togeher and Mary Lou wrote the arrangement. Another one I liked very well was 'You know Baby' which the composer Frank Lewis cooperated with Mary Lou and gave me a few extra bucks to sing. But my voice was under-recorded because Asch thought that I was singing too loud. His studio was quite small and so was his sound cabin,…
These recordings were made in August 1944, and later Asch recorded two numbers with the singer Josh White and the line-up was Mary Lou, myself, Eddie Dougherty on drums and Jimmy Butts on bass.

September found us rehearsing with a show that was to make a propaganda tour for the re-election of President Franklin D.Roosevelt. Jack "the Bear" Parker was added on drums and the trio became a quartet.
